drug_class: Antihistamine eye drop (ophthalmic antihistamine and mast cell stabilizer)
purpose: Epinastine eye drops are used to relieve itchy eyes caused by allergies. It helps with symptoms like redness, itching, and watering of the eyes that happen when you come into contact with things like pollen, pet dander, or dust. It is meant to be used in the eyes only, not swallowed.
how_it_works: When your body encounters something you are allergic to, it releases a chemical called histamine, which causes itching and irritation. Epinastine works by blocking histamine from attaching to the cells in your eyes, which stops the allergic reaction from causing symptoms. It also helps prevent your eye cells from releasing more of these irritating chemicals in the first place.
common_side_effects: Mild burning or stinging when you first put the drops in, headache, runny nose, feeling like something is in your eye, and mild eye redness. These effects are usually short-lived and not serious.
warnings: Do not wear contact lenses while your eyes are red or irritated. If you do wear contacts, wait at least 10 minutes after using the drops before putting them back in. Do not use this medicine if you are allergic to epinastine. Tell your doctor if you are pregnant, breastfeeding, or giving this to a child under 3 years old. Avoid touching the dropper tip to your eye or any surface to prevent contamination.
typical_dosing: The usual dose for adults and children 3 years and older is one drop in each affected eye twice a day, roughly every 12 hours. Keep using it for as long as you are around allergens, even if your symptoms feel better. Always wash your hands before using the eye drops.
